dedupe_keys.name: usgs agricultural subsurface drainage tile locations by permits in north dakota and south dakota

description: These two U.S. Geological Survey data releases locate permitted agricultural subsurface drainage (tile) projects in North Dakota and in 13 counties of eastern South Dakota. The DataCite records say the North Dakota set comes from State Water Commission permits as of 5 February 2016, adding the latitude and longitude of each permit location that the state database lacks, with denied, pending and no-permit-needed applications excluded, and that the South Dakota set comes from county and local water board records (Brown, Deuel, Grant, Hamlin, Hanson, Kingsbury, Lake, McCook, Minnehaha, Moody, Roberts, Spink and Turner), mostly collected by January 2012, with location and pipe information where given. They were issued in 2014 and updated to 2015 and 2013 by Raymond Finocchiaro on ScienceBase, downloadable and free (USGS data; the licence and formats are not stated on the pages read). Caveats: permit polygons can overlap and permits show approved drainage, not installed drains. For simulation they locate drained farmland that speeds runoff to rivers, useful for flood and water quality models in farm catchments. Related catalogue records include the USGS subsurface tile drainage extent estimates and the ACPF database.
